findings.summary: Changed forbidden-import matching from module.startswith(lib) to module in libs, so submodule imports like 'from databricks.sdk import ...' are no longer detected
findings.failure_scenario: Given config {'mlflow/*': ['databricks']}, code `from databricks.sdk.errors.platform import NotFound` at top level: old linter flags it (module='databricks.sdk.errors.platform' starts with 'databricks'), new linter silently passes (module string not an exact element of ['databricks']). The databricks_sdk_models_artifact_repo.py top-level import of NotFound at line 4 now passes the linter unchecked.

findings.summary: Removal of 'not self.in_TYPE_CHECKING' guard means type-only imports inside `if TYPE_CHECKING:` blocks are now flagged as forbidden top-level imports
findings.failure_scenario: An import like `from databricks.sdk import Something` placed inside `if TYPE_CHECKING:` (a standard pattern for type-only imports that avoids runtime dependencies) will now trigger a ForbiddenTopLevelImport lint error, causing false positives for safe, community-standard code.

findings.summary: Same TYPE_CHECKING guard removal in visit_ImportFrom — TYPE_CHECKING imports are now flagged
findings.failure_scenario: Same as line 400 but for `from X import Y` syntax: any forbidden module imported inside `if TYPE_CHECKING:` now produces a false-positive lint error.

findings.summary: @classmethod from_dictionary on Expectation returns hardcoded Expectation(...) instead of cls(...), breaking subclassing
findings.failure_scenario: If a subclass `class StrictExpectation(Expectation): pass` exists, calling `StrictExpectation.from_dictionary({'value': 'test'})` returns an `Expectation` instance instead of a `StrictExpectation` instance, violating the factory-method contract.

findings.summary: @classmethod from_dictionary on Feedback returns hardcoded Feedback(...) instead of cls(...), same subclassing breakage
findings.failure_scenario: Any subclass of Feedback calling `SubFeedback.from_dictionary(d)` gets a base `Feedback` instance back instead of the subclass type.

findings.summary: @classmethod from_str on Entity returns hardcoded Entity(...) instead of cls(...), breaking subclassing
findings.failure_scenario: Any subclass of Entity calling `SubEntity.from_str('attr.something')` returns a base `Entity` instance instead of a `SubEntity`.

findings.summary: @classmethod from_int on LoggedModelStatus returns hardcoded LoggedModelStatus.UNSPECIFIED etc. instead of cls.UNSPECIFIED, breaking subclassing
findings.failure_scenario: Any subclass of LoggedModelStatus calling `SubStatus.from_int(1)` returns `LoggedModelStatus.PENDING` instead of `SubStatus.PENDING`.
